analysis.title: The Global Point
key_insights: Global Sporting Goods (Top Call): total StockX sneaker resale volumes fell -0.8% MoM in October after -0.5% on the prior 3-month average, the 12th consecutive monthly decline. Excluding NKE, the market fell -2.2% MoM (after -2.9% prior 3m average).

Brand share of StockX resale volume in October: ADS -25bps MoM (biggest decline of the brands tracked), PUM -2bps, NKE +39bps (the 8th consecutive monthly increase). NKE's own resale volumes fell a more moderate -0.2% MoM.
Sporting goods catalysts: NKE's capital markets day (CMD) on 16-17 Nov and JD Sports' 3Q27 trading update on 19 Nov.

NVDA preview: reports October-quarter earnings on 11/17. Citi expects a modest EPS beat on results and guide, with higher sales offset by lower gross margins from an HBM price increase, and expects Nvidia to reiterate its FY28E (CY27E) revenue outlook of 70% Y/Y growth.

NVDA investor focus: 2028 order visibility and backlog conversion (especially neocloud customers), supply constraints, the Rubin ramp, and a CEO investigation. Citi keeps estimates, trims its target price 10% to $285 (19x CY27E P/E vs prior 21x, for lower market multiples and long-term CEO sustainability risk), and maintains Buy.

China AIDC tech tour (visited AMEC Lingang, BIRENTECH, Montage, Sensetime on 9 Nov): domestic chips are used for inferencing today, with 2027-28 products expected to improve and possibly carry localized HBM. The main constraint is chip manufacturing and HBM supply. Buy reiterated on AMEC and Montage.

Hong Kong property: Citi expects sector leadership to rotate from landlords to residential developers in 2027E on falling supply, end-user demand and higher rents and prices. It forecasts home prices up another 6% y/y, with primary sales of c.22k units against completions of 15-16k.

Hong Kong property pecking order: residential > core office > luxury retail > suburban retail > non-core office. Picks: SHKP and Henderson Land (residential), Swire Properties (prime office and luxury retail), Link REIT (capital recycling).

Turkish Airlines: after 3Q26 results Citi raises FY26E EBITDAR 6% on lower fuel and cuts FY27-29E EBITDAR 2-4% on a c3ppt rise in non-fuel unit costs. PT moves up to TL315 from TL300 on a weaker lira. Rating stays Neutral.

Western Europe apparel and footwear: ahead of NKE's CMD (16-17 Nov), Citi expects NKE to confirm strategy for sportswear, Jordan and Greater China. A strong product pipeline and premium wholesale commitment would be a positive read-across for JD Sports. For ADS/PUM the focus is China strategy and product pipeline.
Marks & Spencer 2026 CMD: discussion centered on the margin opportunity in Fashion, Home & Beauty. Five takeaways are listed in the full note.
DSV: Citi's 4Q26E adjusted operating profit of DKK7,064m is c.4% above Bloomberg consensus, mainly in Air and Sea. Air and Sea GP of DKK9,721m compares with consensus of DKK9,229m.

DSV drivers: the TAC air freight index points to a strong peak season, September-October container rates (c.2/3 of 4Q26E recognized rates) are well above June-August, and October German freight vehicle miles rose y/y, supporting Road.

Notable target price cuts over 10%: Sea (SE) to $136 from $176, Wonik IPS to W134,000 from W165,000, Vista Energy to $70 from $88, Hudson Pacific to $10 from $15, Nitto Boseki to ¥3,700 from ¥5,200, GMR Solutions to $15 from $17, Lucid to $9 from $11.

sector_views.rationale: Citi prefers residential developers over landlords for 2027E on falling supply, end-user demand and higher home rents and prices.
Resale volumes are shrinking, but NKE keeps gaining share while ADS and PUM lose it.
Air, sea and road end markets are improving into 4Q26E, with a strong peak season in air freight.

earnings_insights: NVDA reports October-quarter earnings on 11/17. Citi expects a modest EPS beat on both results and guide (Citi estimate, not a print), with higher sales offset by lower gross margins from the HBM price increase.

DSV 4Q26E (Citi estimate, not yet reported): adjusted operating profit DKK7,064m, c.4% above Bloomberg consensus. GP/TEU DKK4,183 is c.4% above consensus. Air GP/ton DKK9,218 is c.5% above consensus and +3% vs 3Q26. Air and Sea GP DKK9,721m vs BBG consensus DKK9,229m.
Turkish Airlines reported 3Q26 results last week. Citi raised FY26E EBITDAR 6% on lower fuel and cut FY27-29E EBITDAR 2-4% on a c3ppt rise in assumed non-fuel unit costs.
NKE (1Q27 results, 1-Oct) showed sportswear and the Jordan brand as a high-single-digit drag on consolidated sales growth. NKE's CMD is on 16-17 Nov.
JD Sports 3Q27 trading update is due 19 Nov.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Citi expects Nvidia to reiterate this prior outlook at its 11/17 results.
Citi forecasts another 6% rise on falling supply and sustained end-user demand.
Citi lists this as a macro factor that may normalize in 2027E.

crypto_views: Securitize Corp (SECZ.N), a tokenization platform, was upgraded to Buy, High Risk from Neutral, High Risk, with a $14.00 target. The note gives no further detail.
risk_factors: NVDA: supply constraints, the Rubin ramp, backlog conversion with neocloud customers, a CEO investigation and long-term CEO sustainability risk, plus HBM price increases that pressure gross margin.
China AIDC: supply constraints in chip manufacturing and HBM limit domestic compute localization.
Hong Kong property: possible 2027E normalization of Rmb/HK$ forex, record IPOs and talent inflows, and an uncertain US rate path.
Turkish Airlines: higher non-fuel unit costs, with a weaker lira lifting the target price in local terms.
charts_described: Charts show Adidas and Nike (Nike + Jordan + Converse) share of StockX sporting goods resale volume on a 12-month rolling basis through Oct-26. The text gives only the MoM share changes, not the plotted levels.
Chart of NVDA P/E (FY2) valuation over time. The text gives only the 19x CY27E target multiple.
